transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... well, I hope I'm not wasting your time. I feel a little silly even bringing it up, to be honest. 

But I'm a carpenter, and lately, I just... I can't seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. I mean, maybe it's just normal for someone my age, right? But it's getting to where if a saw starts up in the shop, or somebody just walks past the office, or even if I just get a passing thought in my head about another job... it just pulls me right off what I'm supposed to be doing. And then the whole day just completely gets away from me. 

I try really hard to stay on track, I promise, but it's just been a struggle. Is that... is that the sort of thing I should be talking to you about? Does that make sense?
When you think back to when you were a child in school, did you already have trouble paying attention?

Oh, um... well, I suppose... yes. I mean, I really tried to be a good student, I promise I did. But, um... looking back, even in grade school, like definitely before I was 12 or so... my teachers were always telling my mother that I was bright. They always made sure to say I was a bright girl! 

But... they also said I could be a bit careless. I'd, you know, accidentally lose my homework, or I'd forget the instructions they just gave us. And I guess I spent a lot of time just staring out the window instead of finishing my seatwork. I really wasn't trying to be a bad student or anything, my mind would just sort of drift off. 

I hope that answers your question... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do these attention problems cause trouble for you in more than one part of your life, not just at work?

Well, um... I guess you could say it happens at home, too. I mean, it's not like I'm a complete disaster or anything! I try my best to keep everything running smoothly. But, um... my husband has had to start handling all the bills and the important mail. I just... I kept misplacing the papers, or I'd completely forget what needed to be paid and when. I felt so awful about it, but he's been very patient. He just took over the reminders and things so I wouldn't have to worry.

And at work... well, like I said, I'm a carpenter, and I take a lot of pride in my work. But lately, um... I've made a few little mistakes here and there. Just small things, mostly! But it has meant we've had to redo some work, and I think it's cost us a couple of commissions. The crew... well, they're great guys, but I think they're a little hesitant to let me handle the scheduling or the material orders right now. I can't really blame them. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is... I really do try my best to keep on top of things. Is that the kind of information you were looking for?
Do you spend a lot of your day worrying about many different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier, really. I mean, I try to look on the bright side of things! I definitely don't sit around fretting all day, I promise. 

Of course, I care about doing a good job and making sure my husband is happy, but it's not like I'm constantly anxious or panicking about things that haven't happened yet. I just try to take things one day at a time, you know? 

I hope that's okay to say. I just... I don't want you to think I'm a bundle of nerves or anything. Does that answer your question alright?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say so. I mean, sure, I get a little frustrated with myself when I mess up a measurement at the shop or lose track of the mail, but... I'm really not depressed, I promise! 

I try to keep a very positive attitude. I have a wonderful husband and I really do love my trade, so I don't have any reason to be gloomy. I just try to keep a smile on my face and do my best every day. 

I hope that's okay... I just wouldn't want you to think I'm unhappy or complaining about my life. Am I... am I giving you the right kind of information?
Have these attention problems clearly interfered with your ability to function at work or at home?

Well, um... I guess if you really look at it, maybe they have a little bit. I mean, I don't want to sound like I can't handle my own life! I really do try to keep everything together. But, um... like I mentioned before, at work, my little mix-ups have caused some rework, and... well, we've lost a couple of commissions because of it. And the guys on the crew, they're so sweet, but they've kind of stopped asking me to handle the scheduling or ordering the materials. Which is fine! I understand why. 

And then at home... well, my husband is just wonderful, but he did have to take over all the bills and the important reminders. I just kept losing the papers or forgetting when things were due. It's just a little bit embarrassing to admit, you know? I really want to be helpful and do my part. 

I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm completely helpless... I really do try my hardest. Does that answer what you were asking?
